answer: An oasis protocol binds recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments to copper staking collateral, so a cloned identity carries only a slashed ember of prior attestation and is exposed by sequential zero-knowledge verifiable delay proofs. The slashing penalty for m Sybil pseudonyms exceeds their expected stake reward once m exceeds threshold tau, rendering identity cloning computationally infeasible, giving negative expected attack utility and a robust Nash equilibrium.
